tierWindow.goal: Put searching into practice as a craft: plan a search, build the terms that drive it, and construct and refine it in a library discovery service.
tierWindow.cognitiveDemand: Application and construction (apply, construct, refine), with reasoned choices, rather than recall or description.
tierWindow.taskComplexity: Multi-step but bounded: a realistic search carried through from plan to keywords to a refined discovery-service search; one search strategy at a time.
tierWindow.autonomy: Moderate scaffolding; worked examples that model the craft; checks ask the learner to choose and refine rather than only recognise.

decidedValue.priorExperienceAnchor: The learner already knows what academic searching is and why it matters (the introductory tier, 'searching as a discipline'). They have run basic searches but tend to type a few words into a search box and take what comes back. This course assumes that starting point and builds the craft of searching deliberately; it does not re-teach what searching is.

decidedValue.signpostBody: The course has three short lessons that follow the order of a real search. First, planning your search: the thinking you do before you type. Second, identifying keywords: building the terms that drive the search. Third, searching your discovery service: combining and refining those terms into results you can use. Work through them in order; each builds on the one before.
decidedValue.signpostInstruction: Work through the three lessons in order.
decidedValue.overview:
This short course is about the craft of finding sources: how to search well, not just how to search. By the end you will be able to plan a search before you begin, build the keywords and synonyms that drive it, and construct and refine a real search in your library discovery service using Boolean logic and limiters.

Searching is one of the most important academic skills, and most students do it far less effectively than they could. A planned, well-built search finds better sources in less time, and better sources make better work. This course turns searching from guesswork into a strategy you control.
decidedValue.courseOutcomesFraming: Three course outcomes framed up front: plan a search, build the keywords that drive it, construct and refine it in a discovery service.

practiceConnection.academic: Searching well underpins almost everything you do at university. Every essay, report and project begins with finding the right sources, and a strong search saves hours and raises the quality of what you read. Build the craft now and it serves every assignment of your degree, and the research that professional work later asks of you.

grounding.note: W-OPEN states the three course outcomes and why they matter (AL-5)

decidedValue.whereNextBody: Two directions build on this. Going deeper: the advanced finding and using sources course takes you into subject databases, Google Scholar and citation searching, and into evaluating sources in depth. Going wider: the same craft underpins Academic Writing, Criticality and Researching, where you put the sources you find to work.
decidedValue.summary: You have reached the end of the course. Searching is no longer something you do by typing a few words and hoping. You can plan a search before you begin, setting an objective and choosing the source type and date range that fit. You can build the keywords and synonyms that drive it. And you can construct and refine a real search in your discovery service, using Boolean operators, phrases, wildcards and limiters to control what comes back. Look back at the confidence check: comparing where you started with where you are now shows how far this has moved.

practiceConnection.academic: From here, searching well is something you practise in every module. Each assignment that sends you to the literature, each time you plan before you type, each search you refine rather than abandon, is this craft at work. It is also what research and professional life reward: the ability to find the right evidence quickly, and to know it is the right evidence.
